q: According to the Genesis account of creation, God created the firmament on the _____ day.
explanation: On the second day, God created the expanse (firmament) to separate the waters from the waters (Genesis 1:6-8).

q: God's sovereignty is best demonstrated in the creation story by His ability to _____.
explanation: God's sovereignty is shown through 'Ex Nihilo' creation—bringing things into existence simply by commanding them to be.

q: The primary reason why Joseph's brothers hated him was because _____.
opts: he was born in old age
explanation: Genesis 37:3-4 states that because Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons, the brothers hated him and could not speak peaceably to him.

q: In the call of Abraham, God's command to 'Go from your country...' was a test of his _____.
explanation: Abraham's departure for an unknown land demonstrated absolute trust and faith in God's promise.

q: Moses was reluctant to lead the Israelites out of Egypt because he _____.
explanation: In Exodus 4:10, Moses complained to God that he was 'slow of speech and of tongue'.

q: The Egyptian king who 'did not know Joseph' oppressed the Israelites because _____.
explanation: The King feared that the Israelites were becoming more numerous and powerful than the Egyptians (Exodus 1:9-10).

q: The Tenth Plague that finally broke Pharaoh's heart was the _____.
explanation: The death of every first-born in Egypt, including Pharaoh's son, forced the King to release the Israelites.

q: The Ten Commandments were given to Moses on Mount _____.
explanation: Exodus 19-20 records the giving of the Decalogue (Ten Commandments) on Mount Sinai.

q: The Ark of the Covenant was a symbol of God's _____ among the Israelites.
explanation: The Ark represented the dwelling place and the constant presence of God with His people.

q: The first king of Israel was _____.
explanation: Saul, the son of Kish, was anointed by Samuel as the first king following the people's demand.

q: David's refusal to kill Saul in the cave showed his _____.
explanation: David believed that it was wrong to touch the 'Lord's anointed', regardless of Saul's behavior.

q: Solomon asked God for _____ to rule his people effectively.
explanation: At Gibeon, Solomon asked for a 'discerning heart' (wisdom) to govern the vast people of Israel.

q: The prophet who challenged the 450 prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel was _____.
explanation: Elijah sought to prove that Yahweh is the only true God by calling down fire on the altar.

q: Amos emphasized that true worship must be accompanied by _____.
explanation: Amos 5:24 says, 'But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream'.

q: The message of Prophet Hosea focused primarily on the _____ of God.
explanation: Hosea's marriage to Gomer served as a metaphor for God's steadfast love for unfaithful Israel.

q: Nebuchadnezzar was the king of _____ who destroyed Jerusalem.
explanation: Babylon, under Nebuchadnezzar, captured Jerusalem and took the Jews into exile.

q: The wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt after the exile under the leadership of _____.
explanation: Nehemiah was the cupbearer who returned to Jerusalem specifically to lead the reconstruction of the walls.

q: Daniel and his three friends refused to eat the King's meat because it _____.
explanation: The food was likely offered to idols or was not prepared according to Jewish dietary laws (kosher).

q: Jesus was born in Bethlehem during the reign of King _____.
explanation: Herod the Great was the King of Judea at the time of Jesus' birth and ordered the massacre of the innocents.

q: The forerunner of Jesus was _____.
explanation: John the Baptist was sent to 'prepare the way of the Lord' and preach repentance.

q: Jesus was baptized in River _____.
explanation: John the Baptist baptized Jesus in the Jordan River to 'fulfill all righteousness'.

q: In the temptation of Jesus, the devil asked Him to turn stones into bread to test His _____.
explanation: The temptation 'If you are the Son of God...' was an attempt to make Jesus use His divine power for selfish physical needs.

q: The first four disciples called by Jesus were _____.
explanation: Peter, Andrew, James, and John were all fishermen at the Sea of Galilee.

q: The miracle of the feeding of the five thousand demonstrated Jesus as the _____.
explanation: This miracle is often linked to Jesus' discourse on being the Bread that came down from heaven.

q: The parable of the Good Samaritan was told to explain the meaning of _____.
explanation: Jesus told it in response to a lawyer's question: 'And who is my neighbor?'

q: In the parable of the Prodigal Son, the father's reaction shows God's _____.
explanation: The father running to meet the son illustrates God's eagerness to forgive and restore repentant sinners.

q: Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem was on a _____.
explanation: Riding a donkey fulfilled the prophecy of Zechariah 9:9 and symbolized Jesus as a Prince of Peace, not a war-lord.

q: The disciple who betrayed Jesus was _____.
explanation: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver.

q: At the Last Supper, the wine symbolized Jesus' _____.
explanation: Jesus stated that the cup represented His blood, which was to be shed for the remission of sins.

q: The Roman Governor who sentenced Jesus to death was _____.
explanation: Pilate found no guilt in Jesus but succumbed to the pressure of the crowd to have Him crucified.

q: Jesus was crucified at a place called Golgotha, which means _____.
explanation: Golgotha is an Aramaic word meaning 'Skull', referring to the shape of the hill or its use as a site for executions.

q: The first person to see the risen Christ according to Mark was _____.
explanation: Mark 16:9 records that Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom He had cast seven demons.

q: The Great Commission instructs disciples to go and make disciples of _____.
explanation: In Matthew 28:19, Jesus commanded the disciples to go and teach 'all nations'.

q: The Holy Spirit descended on the disciples on the day of _____.
explanation: Acts 2 describes the arrival of the Holy Spirit on the Day of Pentecost, 50 days after Easter.

q: The first Christian martyr was _____.
explanation: Stephen was stoned to death for his witness to Christ, as recorded in Acts 7.

q: Saul of Tarsus was converted on the road to _____.
explanation: Saul was blinded by a great light and heard the voice of Jesus while traveling to Damascus to persecute Christians.

q: The first place where believers were called Christians was _____.
explanation: Acts 11:26 notes that it was in Antioch that the name 'Christian' first came into use.

q: The Jerusalem Council was held primarily to discuss _____.
explanation: Acts 15 records the debate over whether Gentile converts needed to be circumcised and follow the Law of Moses.

q: According to Paul in Galatians, the fruit of the Spirit includes the following EXCEPT _____.
explanation: Wisdom is listed as a 'gift' of the Spirit in 1 Corinthians 12, while the others are listed as 'fruit' in Galatians 5.

q: Paul's letter to Philemon was an appeal for the pardon of _____.
explanation: Onesimus was a runaway slave who had become a Christian under Paul's ministry.

q: James teaches that 'Faith without _____ is dead'.
explanation: James 2:26 emphasizes that true faith must be reflected in practical actions.

q: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus called his followers the _____ of the earth.
explanation: Jesus used 'salt' and 'light' to describe the transformative influence Christians should have on society.

q: The specific sin of Ananias and Sapphira was _____.
explanation: They kept back part of the proceeds of a land sale while pretending to give the full amount to the church.

q: Paul was a citizen of _____ by birth.
explanation: Paul often used his Roman citizenship to appeal to higher courts and protect himself from arbitrary punishment.

q: The theme of the book of Amos is God's _____.
explanation: Amos was a prophet of social justice who condemned the oppression of the poor by the wealthy in Israel.

q: The 'Great Commandment' according to Jesus is to love _____.
explanation: Jesus taught that loving God with all one's heart, soul, and mind is the first and greatest commandment.

q: Who was the queen that visited Solomon to test his wisdom?
explanation: The Queen of Sheba came with hard questions and was overwhelmed by Solomon's wisdom and wealth.

q: The name 'Peter' given to Simon by Jesus means _____.
explanation: Jesus called him 'Petros' (rock) and said upon this rock He would build His church.

q: Elijah was taken up to heaven in a _____.
explanation: 2 Kings 2:11 records that a chariot and horses of fire appeared, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind.

q: The person who helped Jesus carry the cross was _____.
explanation: Simon of Cyrene, an African, was compelled by Roman soldiers to carry the cross.

q: God's promise to Noah was sealed with a _____.
explanation: The rainbow was the sign of the covenant that God would never again destroy the earth with a flood.

q: The first murder in the Bible was committed by _____.
explanation: Cain killed his brother Abel out of jealousy because God accepted Abel's offering and not his.

q: Hagar was the handmaid of _____.
explanation: Sarah gave her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abraham to bear a child on her behalf.

q: The son of Abraham through Hagar was _____.
explanation: Ishmael was Abraham's first son, though Isaac was the son of the promise through Sarah.

q: The city of Jericho was captured by _____.
explanation: Joshua led the Israelites in the miraculous conquest of Jericho where the walls fell down.

q: Samson's strength was in his _____.
explanation: As a Nazirite, Samson's strength was tied to his vow, symbolized by his uncut hair.

q: Gideon defeated the Midianites with only _____ men.
explanation: God reduced Gideon's army to 300 to show that the victory belonged to the Lord and not human strength.

q: The mother of Samuel was _____.
explanation: Hannah was barren but prayed fervently at Shiloh, promising to dedicate her son to the Lord.

q: Solomon's temple was built in the city of _____.
explanation: Jerusalem was the political and religious capital where the temple was situated.

q: The 'Valley of dry bones' vision was seen by Prophet _____.
explanation: Ezekiel saw the vision of dry bones coming to life, symbolizing the restoration of Israel.

q: Jesus healed a man born blind by using _____.
explanation: John 9 records that Jesus spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and put it on the man's eyes.

q: The 'Man of Sorrows' is a Messianic title found in the book of _____.
explanation: Isaiah 53 contains the 'Suffering Servant' prophecy, describing the Messiah as a man of sorrows.

q: Jesus was born in a _____.
explanation: Because there was no room in the inn, Mary laid the baby Jesus in a manger.

q: The disciple who doubted the resurrection until he saw Jesus was _____.
explanation: Thomas is often called 'Doubting Thomas' because he demanded physical proof of Jesus' wounds.

q: The gift of the Magi included gold, frankincense, and _____.
explanation: Myrrh was an expensive ointment used for burial, symbolizing Jesus' future death.

q: Paul wrote the letter to the Romans to explain the doctrine of _____.
explanation: Romans is Paul's most theological letter, focusing on how humans are made right with God through faith in Christ.

q: The 'New Covenant' was prophesied by _____.
explanation: Jeremiah 31:31 mentions the days when God would make a new covenant written on the hearts of people.

q: The last book of the New Testament is _____.
explanation: The Book of Revelation contains the apocalyptic visions of John regarding the end of the age.

q: The Christian virtue of 'Agape' means _____.
explanation: Agape is the highest form of love, representing God's selfless love for humanity.

q: In Christian teaching, 'Civic Responsibility' involves _____.
explanation: Romans 13 and 1 Peter 2 emphasize that Christians should be good citizens and respect governing authorities.
